# Control Narrative: Aggregate Conveying Line (LINE-01)

**Document status:** Draft A for review. Tag numbers for signals are provisional until they are aligned to the instrument index. Every value you did not give me is marked TBD in the setpoint list. I did not invent any.

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

The line moves aggregate from the hopper to the stockpile. The flow order is: hopper → VF-1 → CV-1 → CV-2 → CR-1 → CV-3 → stockpile.

This narrative covers start, stop, and protection of VF-1, CV-1, CV-2, CR-1, and CV-3. It does not cover feed rate control, hopper level, or stockpile management.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LINE-001 | The system must accept a start command only from the control room HMI. | FAT: try to start from each other source |
| FR-LINE-002 | The STOP LINE command must be available on the HMI in every state except Stopped. | FAT: demonstration |

## 2. Equipment and signals

Use the instrument index for ranges and scaling. Signal tags follow the provisional pattern below.

| Signal | Tag pattern | Fitted to |
|---|---|---|
| Zero-speed switch | SSL-xxx | CV-1, CV-2, CV-3 |
| Misalignment, alarm stage | MSH-xxx | CV-1, CV-2, CV-3 |
| Misalignment, trip stage | MSHH-xxx | CV-1, CV-2, CV-3 |
| Pull-cord switch group | HS-xxx-PC | CV-1, CV-2, CV-3 |
| Plugged-chute switch | LSH-xxx | CV-1, CV-2, CV-3 (at discharge) |
| Motor current | JIT-CR1 | CR-1 (CT) |
| Lube oil pressure switch | PSL-CR1 | CR-1 |
| Warning horn and beacon | XA-LINE | Line |

## 3. States and transitions

The line is a state-based unit (ISA-106). VF-1, the conveyors, and CR-1 are equipment modules under the line.

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Stopped | All units stopped. No trip active. |
| Starting | Warning or start sequence in progress. |
| Running | All units proved running. |
| Stopping | Normal stop sequence in progress. |
| Tripped | A protection trip is latched. Units stop per the trip response. |

| ID | From → To | Permissive or condition | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Stopped → Starting | All start permissives (P-LINE) true | Operator | Operator-initiated, automatic sequence |
| T2 | Starting → Running | All five units proved running | Automatic | Automatic |
| T3 | Starting → Stopped | CANCEL START pushed during warning; no unit has moved | Operator | Manual |
| T4 | Starting → Stopping | STOP LINE pushed after a unit has started | Operator | Operator-initiated, automatic sequence |
| T5 | Running → Stopping | STOP LINE pushed | Operator | Operator-initiated, automatic sequence |
| T6 | Starting, Running, Stopping → Tripped | Any trip in section 6 | Automatic | Automatic |
| T7 | Stopping → Stopped | Zero speed confirmed on all units | Automatic | Automatic |
| T8 | Tripped → Stopped | All units at zero speed, cause cleared, RESET pushed | Operator | Manual |

**Start permissives (P-LINE)**
- No trip is latched.
- All pull-cord switches are reset.
- All misalignment trip switches are healthy.
- No plugged-chute switch is active.
- PSL-CR1 shows lube pressure healthy.
- JIT-CR1 signal quality is good.
- Every drive is available and in remote.
- HMI communication is healthy.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LINE-010 | The system must refuse a start if any P-LINE item is false. | FAT: force each item false |
| FR-LINE-011 | The HMI must show each false P-LINE item by name. | FAT: inspection |
| FR-LINE-012 | The system must not leave the Tripped state without a manual RESET. | FAT: demonstration |

## 4. Regulatory control

This module has no control loops. The VF-1 feed rate is outside this narrative. See open item OI-05.

## 5. Sequences

The sequences use SqBC and are derived from the state table above.

### 5.1 SQ-LINE-START (transition T1)

The units start against the flow. This puts the receiving unit in motion before it gets material.

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Start XA-LINE (horn and beacon). | Warning time elapsed (SP-LINE-001). | None | If a permissive is lost or CANCEL START is pushed, stop XA-LINE and go to Stopped (T3). |
| S2 | Start CV-3. | SSL-CV3 shows movement. | SP-LINE-002 | Trip CV-3. Abort start. Go to Tripped. |
| S3 | Start CR-1. | Lube pressure healthy and current below the high-current alarm after the start mask. | SP-LINE-002 | Trip CR-1. Stop CV-3. Go to Tripped. |
| S4 | Start CV-2. | SSL-CV2 shows movement. | SP-LINE-002 | Trip CV-2. Stop CR-1 and CV-3 per the trip response. Go to Tripped. |
| S5 | Start CV-1. | SSL-CV1 shows movement. | SP-LINE-002 | Trip CV-1. Stop downstream units per the trip response. Go to Tripped. |
| S6 | Start VF-1. | VF-1 running feedback true. | SP-LINE-002 | Stop VF-1. Alarm. Go to Tripped. |
| S7 | Stop XA-LINE. | All five units proved running. | None | Not applicable. |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LINE-020 | The system must start the units in this order: CV-3, CR-1, CV-2, CV-1, VF-1. | FAT: sequence trace |
| FR-LINE-021 | The system must run XA-LINE for the duration in SP-LINE-001 before it sends a run command to any conveyor. | FAT: timer check, measure first run command |
| FR-LINE-022 | XA-LINE must stay on until S7. | FAT: observation |
| FR-LINE-023 | The system must start the next step only after the previous unit is proved running. | FAT: block each proof in turn |

### 5.2 SQ-LINE-STOP (transitions T4, T5)

The stop sequence empties each unit before it stops. The run-out time of a conveyor starts when its feed stops.

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Stop VF-1. | VF-1 running feedback false. | SP-LINE-009 | Alarm. Continue to S2. |
| S2 | Wait, then stop CV-1. | Run-out time for CV-1 elapsed (SP-LINE-005). | SP-LINE-009 | Alarm "CV-1 not stopped". Hold the sequence. |
| S3 | Wait, then stop CV-2. | Run-out time for CV-2 elapsed (SP-LINE-006). | SP-LINE-009 | Alarm "CV-2 not stopped". Hold the sequence. |
| S4 | Wait, then stop CR-1. | Crusher clear time elapsed (SP-LINE-008). | SP-LINE-009 | Alarm "CR-1 not stopped". Hold the sequence. |
| S5 | Wait, then stop CV-3. | Run-out time for CV-3 elapsed (SP-LINE-007). | SP-LINE-009 | Alarm "CV-3 not stopped". Hold the sequence. |
| S6 | Confirm all units stopped. | SSL-CV1, SSL-CV2, SSL-CV3 show zero speed. CR-1 and VF-1 feedback false. | SP-LINE-009 | Alarm. Stay in Stopping. |

"Hold the sequence" means that the sequence stays at the current step, the alarm stays on, and the operator decides the next action. Do not use this as a trip.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LINE-030 | The system must stop the units in flow order: VF-1, CV-1, CV-2, CR-1, CV-3. | FAT: sequence trace |
| FR-LINE-031 | The system must use a separate run-out time for each conveyor, from the setpoint list. | FAT: change each value, observe |
| FR-LINE-032 | The system must not play the start warning for a normal stop. | FAT: observation |
| FR-LINE-033 | The system must still run the stop sequence in order if STOP LINE is pushed during Starting. | FAT: stop at each start step |

## 6. Interlocks, permissives, and protection

The protection table below is the source for the cause-and-effect chart CE-LINE-001. Move it to the chart at the next revision. Do not copy it into other documents.

### 6.1 Trip response rule

A trip stops the faulted unit and all units upstream of it at the same time. Units downstream of the faulted unit run out and stop in flow order, with their run-out times from the setpoint list.

| Faulted unit | Stops at once | Runs out, then stops |
|---|---|---|
| VF-1 | VF-1 | CV-1, CV-2, CR-1, CV-3 |
| CV-1 | VF-1, CV-1 | CV-2, CR-1, CV-3 |
| CV-2 | VF-1, CV-1, CV-2 | CR-1, CV-3 |
| CR-1 | VF-1, CV-1, CV-2, CR-1 | CV-3 |
| CV-3 | VF-1, CV-1, CV-2, CR-1, CV-3 | None |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LINE-050 | The system must apply the trip response table for every trip in 6.2. | FAT: trip each unit, check the table |
| FR-LINE-051 | The system must latch every trip until RESET. | FAT: clear cause, check the latch stays |
| FR-LINE-052 | The system must record the first trip cause and show it on the HMI. | FAT: trip two causes in sequence |
| FR-LINE-053 | The system must refuse RESET while any unit is moving or while any trip cause is active. | FAT: demonstration |

### 6.2 Protection table

| ID | Signal | Stage | Condition | Action | Delay |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR-LINE-060 | HS-xxx-PC | Trip | Any pull-cord operated | Trip the conveyor with that pull-cord. | None |
| FR-LINE-061 | SSL-xxx | Trip | Zero speed while the conveyor is commanded to run | Trip the conveyor. | SP-LINE-003 (start mask), SP-LINE-004 (running) |
| FR-LINE-062 | MSH-xxx | Alarm | Belt misaligned, first stage | Raise an alarm. No stop. | SP-LINE-010 |
| FR-LINE-063 | MSHH-xxx | Trip | Belt misaligned, second stage | Trip the conveyor. | SP-LINE-011 |
| FR-LINE-064 | LSH-xxx | Trip | Plugged chute at discharge | Trip the conveyor that feeds the chute. | SP-LINE-012 |
| FR-LINE-065 | JIT-CR1 | Alarm | Current above the high-current alarm level | Raise an alarm. No stop. | SP-LINE-016 |
| FR-LINE-066 | JIT-CR1 | Trip | Current above the high-high level | Trip CR-1. | SP-LINE-016 |
| FR-LINE-067 | PSL-CR1 | Permissive | Lube pressure low before start | Refuse the CR-1 start. | None |
| FR-LINE-068 | PSL-CR1 | Trip | Lube pressure low while CR-1 runs | Trip CR-1. | SP-LINE-018 (start), SP-LINE-019 (running) |

**Notes**
- The system must ignore the CR-1 current alarm and trip levels during motor start for the time in SP-LINE-017.
- The pull-cord stop is a personnel protection function. It must stop the drive through the hardwired circuit. The BPCS only reads the status and gives the first-out indication. See the safety requirements specification SRS-LINE (not yet issued) and OI-02.
- Alarm conditions in this section must each have an entry in the rationalized alarm database. This narrative does not restate priorities or setpoints.

### 6.3 Reset

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LINE-070 | After a pull-cord trip, the operator must reset the pull-cord locally before the HMI RESET is accepted. | FAT: demonstration |
| FR-LINE-071 | The system must go to Stopped after RESET only if all P-LINE items are true or shown as false on the HMI. | FAT: demonstration |

## 7. Alarms

Use the rationalized alarm database (ISA-18.2). This narrative lists the conditions only. Each condition in the protection table, each start-proof timeout, and each stop-confirm timeout needs an alarm entry. The line needs one more entry for each of: XA-LINE fault (if feedback is available), HMI comms loss, and drive comms loss.

## 8. Abnormal handling

| ID | Condition | Required behavior | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-LINE-100 | Wire break or lost supply on any protection input | The system must treat the input as active. Pull-cord, zero-speed, and trip-stage inputs trip the unit. The alarm-stage input raises an alarm. | FAT: lift each wire |
| FR-LINE-101 | JIT-CR1 signal out of range or bad quality | The system must refuse the CR-1 start. While CR-1 runs, it must raise an alarm and start a normal stop after SP-LINE-020. | FAT: simulate bad signal |
| FR-LINE-102 | HMI communication loss while the line runs | The line must keep running. The system must raise an alarm. Local stops and pull-cords must stay active. | FAT: disconnect HMI |
| FR-LINE-103 | Communication loss to a drive or remote I/O | The system must trip the affected unit and apply the trip response table. | FAT: disconnect each node |
| FR-LINE-104 | Power loss | All drives must stop and stay stopped when power returns. The line must start in the Tripped state. The operator must push RESET and start the line again. | FAT: power cycle |
| FR-LINE-105 | Controller restart | All run outputs must be off at restart. The system must not restart any unit by itself. | FAT: restart in each state |
| FR-LINE-106 | Fail position | All run outputs must de-energize to stop the unit. | FAT: remove output power |

After a trip or power loss, the belts can hold material. The restart of CR-1 under load is not yet defined. See OI-03.

## 9. Operator interface

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LINE-120 | The HMI must show the line state, the state of each unit, and XA-LINE status. | FAT: inspection |
| FR-LINE-121 | The HMI must have these commands: START LINE, STOP LINE, CANCEL START, RESET. | FAT: inspection |
| FR-LINE-122 | The HMI must show the first-out trip cause and the list of false permissives. | FAT: inspection |
| FR-LINE-123 | The HMI must show the prompt text in the prompt list below. | FAT: inspection |

**Prompts (operations to sign off)**
- Before the start: "Make sure that no person is on or near the line. Push START LINE."
- During the warning: "Warning is on. Push CANCEL START to stop."
- After a pull-cord trip: "Find the cause. Reset the pull-cord at the field location. Push RESET."
- After a stop alarm: "Check the unit in the field. Push STOP LINE again or clear the cause."

## 11. SIS

The BPCS in this narrative is not a safety system. If the risk assessment puts the pull-cord or the crusher protection in a safety function, the SRS defines it. This narrative then references the SRS only.

## Check status

- **Done:** every requirement has an ID and a test method. Numbers are in the setpoint list. Each state has permissives and exits. Each start and stop step has a timeout and failure response, except where the timeout is "None" because the step is a timer or an end step. Bad signal, comms loss, power loss, restart, and fail positions are defined.
- **Not complete:** the setpoint values marked TBD, the STE pass (I wrote to the limits, but you should run the dictionary check), and the open items above.
- **Judgment calls to confirm:** the start order against flow, the trip rule (upstream stops at once, downstream runs out), and treating the pull-cord trip as a conveyor-and-upstream stop. These follow common practice, but your process and safety reviews must approve them.
